title: GCP-6.1 time-master election divergences: C elector has no GPS preference, Python has two divergent electors and 2s default superframe
description: spec/08-gateway-coordination.md GCP-6.1 (L173-175, R-08-023/024), sweep 2026-09-09: 'GPS-equipped gateways use GPS epoch for absolute time. Non-GPS: Elect time master (lowest IID wins); others sync via backbone CoAP.' Evidence: Rust is conformant — elect_time_master GPS-preferred then lowest-IID (rust/lichen-core/src/superframe.rs:220-267; also slot.rs:1688), pinned by gateway_discovery.json time_master_* vectors (discovery.rs tests :571-639) and gateway_coordination.json superframe_sync_gps. DIVERGENT: (1) C lichen_slot_coord_elect_time_master is lowest-IID-only with no GPS preference (lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_slot_coord.c:191) — a GPS gateway can lose election to a non-GPS peer; GPS exists only as a time-source label (coap/include/lichen/coap_slot_coord.h:92-97). (2) Python has TWO divergent electors: rpl/multi_instance.py:205-222 (lowest-IID-only, docstring cites GPS but does not implement it) vs gateway/discovery.py:437-457 (GPS-preferred) — same repo, different answers. (3) Python superframe default 2s (link/channel.py SUPERFRAME_DURATION_US :20) diverges from the 60s default used in gateway info (discovery.py:232) and Rust (superframe.rs:22). (4) Backbone-CoAP time sync for non-GPS gateways ('others sync via backbone CoAP') is not implemented in any stack (python models time strata only, timing/time_sync.py). Suggested placement: C coap_slot_coord.c elector + GPS preference; python unify on one elector + 60s default; backbone time-sync hook. Acceptance: all three stacks elect identically for the same candidate sets (extend gateway_discovery.json time_master_* consumption to C and python-rpl), and a non-GPS gateway converges onto the GPS gateway's epoch via backbone CoAP.
